entries.test: Compare Marcus's earlier listed predictions with publicly documented GPT-5 performance on those problems at launch.
entries.note: The claim describes apparent launch results, preserving the hedge 'appear.'

entries.test: Public development timelines and expenditure reports would establish GPT-5's development duration and cost and the corresponding fieldwide spending.
entries.note: 'To develop' specifies what the elapsed three years measured, which the source leaves unstated.
'Good progress' expresses an evaluation without identifying particular improvements or a standard.

entries.test: Contemporaneous comparative evaluations, including GPT-5 and Grok 4 ARC-AGI-2 scores, would show whether GPT-5 remained within the leading models' performance range.
entries.note: The benchmark example supplies a concrete reading of 'part of the pack.'

entries.test: The GPT-5 launch livestream recording and slides would establish whether OpenAI omitted the ARC-AGI-2 comparison.
entries.note: The omission is factual and checkable; 'marketing rather than science' is an accompanying evaluation.

entries.test: Public expectations documented before launch and comparative GPT-5 capability evaluations would show whether the anticipated major advance materialized.
entries.note: The surrounding benchmark discussion grounds 'huge leap' in capability improvements.

entries.test: Public evaluations of GPT-5's breadth, reliability, and ability to perform unfamiliar intellectual tasks would establish whether it demonstrates general human-level intelligence.
entries.note: Disagreement over precise AGI thresholds does not remove the claim's ordinary capability-based reading.
'May continue' expresses a possibility rather than a firm prediction.

entries.test: Public comparisons of OpenAI's technology and competitors' capabilities and replication progress would show whether GPT-5 provided a clear, defensible technical advantage at launch.
entries.note: 'Technical moat' has an ordinary reading as a technical advantage competitors cannot readily match.

entries.test: The announcement's published graphs would show whether at least two displayed bar lengths inconsistent with their numerical labels and scales.
entries.note: The question presupposes and asserts the graph discrepancies; it asks for their explanation.
'Seems more and more remote' expresses declining perceived likelihood, not a firm prediction that AGI will miss 2027.
Marcus speaks about himself in the third person and retains a 'perhaps' hedge. 'Advanced AI' introduces an unspecified target; the immediate context concerns AGI.
